parts.glance:
Small VIO module from RoboBaton, 8.7 g on a 40 × 20 mm board, with one global-shutter fisheye camera and a TDK ICM-42670-P IMU, hardware-triggered. One hand-held recording in front of an AprilGrid shown on a monitor, recorded by the module's own capture tool and solved as camera + IMU.

Reprojection median0.41 px
cam0 td+1.14 ms
cam0 lever arm30.8 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

One recording, 5 frames per second. The maker's own calibration of the same recording agrees on the rotation (within 0.4°) and on the lever arm across the image (within 2 mm), but not along the optical axis (17 mm here against 9 mm) nor on the time offset (1.1 ms against 0.3 ms). A digital twin of the recording puts the noise on z at about 1 mm, so the gap is systematic; the image stamp convention and the tag size on the monitor are the open questions.

Lens Calibrated field of view

Calibrated field of view, horizontal × vertical. cam0: 126° × ~147°, corners reach 68° from the axis

cam0

We read these from the calibrated lens fit at the image edges, through the principal point (where the optical axis meets the image). ~ marks an axis past where the corners reached, so the fit is extrapolated there. Past the fit means an edge lies beyond where the fit holds, so we give no value.

IMU Gyro–accel time offset t_ga −0.27 ms

Each bar shows a scale as its deviation from 1. IMU model: calyx. t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and accelerometer channels: −0.27 ± 0.07 ms.

The time offsets, to scale. td is the camera–IMU time offset, with t_imu = t_cam + td.

Board shape peak to peak 1.1 mm

The calibration board isn't perfectly flat, so this solve estimated the height of every corner off the flat board along with the calibration. The board's mean plane and tilt belong to its pose, so a flat board shows only noise here.

parts.limits:
• One recording, 5 frames per second. The maker's own calibration of the same recording agrees on the rotation (within 0.4°) and on the lever arm across the image (within 2 mm), but not along the optical axis (17 mm here against 9 mm) nor on the time offset (1.1 ms against 0.3 ms). A digital twin of the recording puts the noise on z at about 1 mm, so the gap is systematic; the image stamp convention and the tag size on the monitor are the open questions.
  • The tag size, 25 mm, is the value in the capture tool's config, not a measurement on the monitor; it scales the lever arm.
  • A double-sphere model fits as well as kb4, but its focal length and xi trade off along a flat valley, so only the projection is comparable between the two.
parts.run: • Camera with the IMU in one solve. Kannala-Brandt (kb4) fisheye intrinsics seeded from a single-camera solve of the same recording and left free; the camera time offset, IMU scale and misalignment and the gyro-to-accel offset t_ga estimated. The board shape is estimated per corner. IMU noise is the ICM-42670-P datasheet value times three. Solved 2026-11-19.
